title: Research plan
description: A reviewable plan for a computational experiment that runs one or more registered models. Domain-agnostic: no model, observable, unit or question is named here. Cross-field invariants that JSON Schema cannot express are listed in x-validator-rules.

question.description: The requester's question, verbatim and unedited.

objective.description: What this plan will establish, in one sentence.

hypothesis.description: The expected outcome and the reasoning for it. Omit for purely exploratory work.

out_of_scope.description: What a reader might reasonably expect this plan to do that it will not do.

sources.description: Every source that fixes part of the configuration.

parameters.description: Every parameter that affects the result, each carrying its provenance.

baseline_run_id.description: Must name a run declared in runs[].

controls.description: Conditions held identical across every compared run, and why.

diagnostics.description: Checks that the result is an artefact of the physics and not of a solver or sampling setting.

success_criteria.description: Declared before execution. At minimum a pass and a fail outcome.

scalar.description: A single parameter value. Arrays and objects are not values; express variation as a sweep.

provenance.description: paper: stated by a source and quotable. inferred: follows from a source but is not written there. assumed: not determinable from any source; the author's choice.

reference.description: Citable identifier: DOI, slug, dataset id, model name and version.

locator.description: Where inside the source: section, table, figure, column, field.

target.description: The specific artefact being reproduced, if any.

quote.description: The passage that fixes the configuration. Required when any parameter cites this source as 'paper'.

opened.description: True only if the content was actually retrieved, not merely cited.

evidence_tier.description: How far this source may be relied on, per the host system's evidence policy.

unit.description: Declared unit, or a sentinel for dimensionless.

basis.description: Why this value. For 'paper', the quoted phrase. For 'inferred', the reasoning. For 'assumed', the justification and the expected cost of being wrong.

source_ref.description: id of an entry in sources[]. Required when provenance is 'paper' or 'inferred'.

graded.description: Whether this parameter counts toward configuration agreement. Only a 'paper' parameter may be graded; grading a value no source fixes is grading a guess.

sensitivity_run_id.description: Run that bounds the cost of this value. Expected whenever provenance is 'assumed'.

expected_effect.description: Direction and rough magnitude of the effect on the observable if this value is wrong.

parameters.description: Overrides for this run. Anything absent takes the plan-level value.

bounds_parameter.description: For stage 'sensitivity', the parameter whose uncertainty this run bounds.

depends_on.description: Run ids that must succeed first.

unit.description: Unit of the observable, or a sentinel for dimensionless metrics.

applies_to.description: Figure or run id this tolerance governs. Omit for the plan-level tolerance.

fixed_before_execution.description: Present to make the commitment explicit and auditable; a tolerance chosen after seeing a result is not a tolerance.

value.description: Null when the reference is a shape or trend rather than a number.

extraction.description: How the reference was obtained; 'digitised' requires read_error.

read_error.description: Uncertainty introduced by extraction, in the same unit. Counts against the tolerance budget.

observable.description: Output column being compared. Must be an output the model declares.

comparability.description: What must hold for the two sides to be differenced at all: same observable, same unit, same conditions.

runs.description: Run ids drawn on this figure.

x.description: Column for the x axis. For swept runs this must be the swept parameter.

ys.description: Additional outputs sharing the same unit.

answers.description: The question this figure alone answers.

required.description: False only for genuinely optional supplementary figures.

distinguish_sources.description: Measured or reference series must not be drawn in the style used for computed series.

interpretation.description: What this outcome would mean, so it cannot be reinterpreted afterwards.

direction.description: Which way this pushes the result if it materialises.

mitigated_by.description: Run or figure ids that bound or detect it.

order.description: Run ids in execution order. Diagnostics that gate interpretation belong first.

resumable.description: Whether completed runs are retained so a later step can be redone without recomputation.

checklist.description: What the reviewer is being asked to confirm, in their own terms.

x-validator-rules: baseline_run_id must equal the id of a run in runs[].
Exactly one run should carry stage 'baseline' unless the plan states why more are needed.
Every parameter.source_ref must match a sources[].id.
Every sources[] entry cited by a 'paper' parameter must have opened == true and a non-empty quote.
Every parameter with provenance 'assumed' must have a sensitivity_run_id, or an explicit waiver recorded in assumptions[].
Every sensitivity_run_id must name a run whose stage is 'sensitivity' and whose bounds_parameter equals that parameter's name.
Every figures[].runs[] entry must match a runs[].id.
For a figure drawing swept runs, figures[].x must equal the sweep.parameter of every run it draws.
Runs compared on one figure must share sweep.parameter, start, stop and points.
figures[].y and every figures[].ys entry must be an output column the named model declares.
Outputs with different units must not share a figure; split them.
comparison.observable must be a declared output of at least one run's model.
success_criteria must contain at least one 'pass' and one 'fail' outcome.
Every tolerance must exist at plan submission; adding or widening one after any run has executed invalidates the reproduction.
The sum of reference_value.read_error and the genuine-disagreement allowance must not exceed the governing tolerance.
execution.order, when present, must be a permutation of runs[].id and must respect every run.depends_on.
No run may execute before the plan reaches an approved phase.
